question_text: A 56-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of pain and swelling in his left leg. He has a history of pancreatic cancer and is currently receiving chemotherapy. Three weeks ago, he had a similar episode in his right arm that resolved without treatment. His temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F). Palpation of the left leg shows a tender, cord-shaped structure medial to the medial condyle of the femur. The overlying skin is erythematous. Which of the following vessels is most likely affected?

        ### Question
        A 56-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of pain and swelling in his left leg. He has a history of pancreatic cancer and is currently receiving chemotherapy. Three weeks ago, he had a similar episode in his right arm that resolved without treatment. His temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F). Palpation of the left leg shows a tender, cord-shaped structure medial to the medial condyle of the femur. The overlying skin is erythematous. Which of the following vessels is most likely affected?

        ### Options
        opa. Anterior tibial artery
opb. Superficial femoral artery
opc. Great saphenous vein
opd. External iliac vein
ope. Deep femoral vein

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Pancreatic cancer -> increased risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) -> chemotherapy-induced hypercoagulability -> 80% CHAIN: Pain and swelling in left leg -> palpable cord-shaped structure -> erythematous skin -> signs of thrombophlebitis -> 70% CHAIN: Tender cord-shaped structure medial to medial condyle of femur -> likely thrombosed vein -> possible deep femoral vein involvement -> 60% CHAIN: History of similar episode in right arm -> resolved without treatment -> possible superficial thrombophlebitis -> 80%
